subject: Request: short-term stability lock for HeliusX-13B integration (Acme Health trial)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term stability lock for HeliusX-13B integration (Acme Health trial)

Hi team,

Quick ask — Acme Health (pilot customer for our Dedicated offering) wants to run a two-week trial starting next Monday using HeliusX-13B-multilang (variant v1.2.0). They need predictability: they asked us to guarantee that the model variant used for the trial won't change mid-trial.

Summary of the request:
- Stability lock (version-level) on HeliusX-13B v1.2.0 for the Acme pilot window (2027-05-31 to 2027-06-14).
- If we must change, we need a planned migration with rollback hooks and a nightly smoke test run against Acme's sample prompts.

Why this matters: Acme is evaluating latency and hallucination characteristics for a clinical triage feature; any mid-trial variant swap would invalidate measurements and jeopardize the pilot. They are sensitive to quality regressions.

What I need from each of you:
- Dev: compatibility and risk assessment (kernel/quantization differences, perf delta). See attached compat_matrix_helx13b.csv for a first-pass.
- Marissa (Ops): capacity/ops impact of holding v1.2.0 in prod for a Reserved Dedicated pool and fallback plan if capacity is constrained.
- Priyom (Telemetry): define the smoke tests / eval set and automation to run nightly during the trial.

Attachments: HeliusX-13B-inference-profile.pdf (model perf profile), compat_matrix_helx13b.csv, stability_lock_request_form.docx (draft).

Target timeline: decision by Thursday EOD so we can confirm with Acme Friday.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Product Lead, Model Intake
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term stability lock for HeliusX-13B integration (Acme Health trial)

Eve,

Thanks for the summary — looked through the attachments. Short answer: we can honor a short-term lock, but there are three technical caveats: 

1) HeliusX v1.2.0 has a known quantization path that uses the legacy KV cache layout. Newer runtime optimizations (batch-kernel fusion rolled out in Apr) assume the new layout. If we pin v1.2.0 on the Dedicated pool, we need a compatibility runtime shim or force the older kernel on that pool. That will cost ~6-8% throughput.

2) We should avoid rolling forward any micro-patches that change tokenizer normalization or token IDs during the trial. That demands a short freeze on tokenizer updates for the Dedicated pool's model image.

3) Memory footprint for v1.2.0 is slightly higher on sequence lengths >1024; we need to size the pool + set a max-seq filter for Acme's pilot traffic (Priyom, can you confirm their expected prompt lengths?).

I'll prepare a config diff and a fallback image (v1.2.0-compat) with the legacy kernel pinned. ETA for config and perf estimates: tomorrow EOD.

- Dev

On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 09:18 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term stability lock for HeliusX-13B integration (Acme Health trial)

Evelyn / Dev,

Operational note — we can allocate a small Dedicated pool for Acme with the constraint of running the legacy kernel, but two operational trade-offs:

- Capacity: to match baseline throughput we will need to add one extra MIG-equivalent (roughly +25% GPU resources) for the pilot window due to the throughput regression Dev mentioned.
- Rollback: if we detect degradation we can fail open to a smaller, quantized variant (HeliusX-8B-q) — but that will change expected quality. If Acme will not accept quality variance, we need an SLA clause for emergency scaling and a pre-approved fallback plan in writing.

I recommend:
1) Approve the short-term lock with explicit constraints (max seq length 1024, traffic cap of 20 rps sustained).
2) Finance/Leadership OK a one-time pilot capacity uplift charge (I can model costs).
3) Priyom to provide smoke tests and expected prompt profile.

If we get a greenlight today I can spin the pool and request the runtime shim from Dev.

— Marissa
Director, Dedicated Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term stability lock for HeliusX-13B integration (Acme Health trial)

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the quick coordination. Acme is comfortable with the constraints you suggested (max seq length ~800 typical for our workflows). Two points from our side: 

1) We do need the model variant to remain identical for the trial window; otherwise our evaluation is invalid.
2) If there is any forced swap, please notify our procurement team 48 hours in advance. We would prefer a documented emergency rollback procedure instead of an unplanned swap.

We can sign a short addendum to the pilot agreement to reflect these asks. Happy to take the proposed SLA/cost uplift.

Tara Singh
Head of Product, Clinical Insights
Acme Health

Thanks everyone — status update and action items: 

1) Dev: please deliver the v1.2.0-compat runtime image and the config diff by tomorrow EOD (INF-8921). If throughput estimate is still +6-8%, include an explicit capacity uplift number.
2) Marissa: provision the Dedicated pool with the legacy kernel forced, cap RPS at 20, max-seq 1024, and add emergency scale policy. Please circulate cost uplift number to Acme procurement.
3) Priyom: finalize the nightly smoke test harness (10 prompts + perf/QA thresholds) and schedule a dry-run Friday. Link results to the Jira in related_links.
4) Legal/Finance (cc as FYI): we will prepare an addendum for Acme that documents the stability lock, notification window, and fallback options.

I'll confirm with Acme once we have the runtime image and pool provisioned. Evelyn
